raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52461.

Under async scheduling (default-on since 0.27) the worker pads each request's
output token id list with `-1` placeholders every step; the real ids are only
patched back in when `logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids` is set. Today that flag
is `bool(custom_logitsprocs)` — i.e. it keys off whether a *CLI* custom
processor is present — which is both an under- and an over-approximation of the
real question ("does any loaded processor read output token *values*?"):

- **Stateful processors registered via `BUILTIN_LOGITS_PROCESSORS` are missed.**
  They silently read `-1` placeholders under async scheduling: full per-step
  overhead is paid, results are wrong, and there is no warning. (The three
  in-tree builtins happen to read only the list *length*, so nothing in-tree
  trips over it today — see the reporter's SynthID-Text watermarking case in the
  issue for a real "reads values" consumer: 8/8 detections with
  `--no-async-scheduling` → 0/8 with async scheduling.)
- **Value-agnostic CLI processors are over-counted**, forcing an unnecessary
  device sync in async mode.

## Change

Add a declarative capability to the interface, mirroring `is_argmax_invariant()`:

```python
@classmethod
def needs_output_token_ids(cls) -> bool:
    return True  # conservative default; out-of-tree processors are correct by default
```

- The three in-tree builtins (`MinP`, `LogitBias`, `MinTokens`) override to
  `False` — they read at most `len(output_tok_ids)`, which is unaffected by
  placeholder *values*.
- `LogitsProcessors` ORs the declaration across every loaded processor (builtin
  + entry-point plugin + CLI) and exposes a single `needs_output_token_ids`.
- `GPUModelRunner` feeds that into `InputBatch` instead of
  `bool(custom_logitsprocs)`. Thinking-budget tracking stays dynamic (unchanged).

Net effect: the async-scheduling repair now runs iff some loaded processor
actually reads token values — fixing the silent-wrong-output case and dropping
the needless sync for value-agnostic processors.

## Not a duplicate of #38199

#38199 targets only the entry-point-plugin gap, via a coarser
`LogitsProcessors.has_custom` flag (true for any non-builtin processor). That
leaves the `BUILTIN_LOGITS_PROCESSORS`-registered stateful case in this issue
still broken, and does not help the value-agnostic over-count. The per-processor
declaration here is a superset covering all three cases; happy to coordinate
landing order with that PR.

## Test

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py -v
```

- Full file: **42 passed** (includes the CUDA `test_logitsprocs[...]` correctness
  cases; run on an RTX A6000).
- Two added unit tests:
  - `test_needs_output_token_ids_declarations` — base default is `True`, the
    three builtins declare `False`.
  - `test_build_logitsprocs_aggregates_output_token_ids_gate` — the aggregated
    gate is `False` for builtins-only and for a value-agnostic custom processor,
    and `True` once a value-reading custom processor is loaded.

No in-tree model output changes (the builtins keep identical behavior; only the
async-scheduling repair *gating* changes), so model evals are N/A; the
end-to-end correctness win is the reporter's SynthID watermarking measurements
in the issue, which I'd be glad to help re-validate.

## Note

This change was developed with AI assistance. I have reviewed every changed
line, understand the change end-to-end, and ran the tests above myself.

🚀

### End-to-end validation under async scheduling

Ran a discriminating A/B on GPU (RTX A6000, `facebook/opt-125m`, `enforce_eager`,
async scheduling on). A probe `LogitsProcessor` registered via
`BUILTIN_LOGITS_PROCESSORS` snapshots each request's `output_tok_ids` from
`apply()` (single-process, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`). Only the probe's
`needs_output_token_ids()` declaration differs between runs:

| `needs_output_token_ids()` | observed `output_tok_ids` in `apply()` | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `True` (this PR's default for out-of-tree procs) | `[5] → [5, 812] → [5, 812, 9] → …` (real ids) | correct |
| `False` (today's behavior for builtin-registered procs) | `[-1] → [-1, -1] → [-1, -1, -1] → …` | silently reads placeholders |

Both runs produce identical output text (the probe only observes), so this
isolates the output-token-id view. The `False` case reproduces the exact silent
failure from the issue; with the declaration wired through the gate, the async
`-1` repair runs and the processor sees real ids.

### Why this is a V1-runner fix (and V2 does not need the same change)

The V2 model runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) does not run
custom/plugin logits processors at all: `_get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features`
lists `"custom logits processors"` as unsupported whenever
`model_config.logits_processors` or a `vllm.logits_processors` entry point is
present (`vllm/config/vllm.py:2447-2450`), so those configs fall back to the V1
runner. The gate this PR fixes lives on the V1 path, which is exactly where such
processors execute. (The e2e forces `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` only because
`opt-125m` happens to default to V2; a real custom/plugin processor forces V1 on
its own.)

### Unit + regression

`python -m pytest tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py -v` → **42 passed**
(includes the CUDA `test_logitsprocs[...]` cases), plus the two added unit tests.
`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the touched files.

Good catch — fixed in 48c70dc. I moved `build_logitsprocs` back inside the `with self.jit_warmup_registry.activate():` block (right before the `InputBatch(...)` construction), so any warmup providers a processor's `__init__` registers are captured exactly as they were before this PR. The gate still reads `logitsprocs.needs_output_token_ids` — the only change vs. main is that the built object is now a local instead of an inline argument, and it's constructed within the same context.

No in-tree processor registers warmup providers today, but keeping construction inside the context makes it robust regardless, and avoids reasoning about registry internals.

Thanks for the production numbers (8/8, mean-g z 8.77) — that's a great data point. If a maintainer wants an extra signal before merge, an A/B of your SynthID setup against this branch would be very welcome.

Re-validated after the warmup-context fix (48c70dc), on the same RTX A6000 setup:

- `pytest tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py` → **42 passed** (incl. the CUDA cases) + the two added unit tests.
- V1 async-scheduling e2e A/B still discriminating end-to-end (the probe now goes through `GPUModelRunner.__init__` → `with self.jit_warmup_registry.activate(): build_logitsprocs(...); InputBatch(...)`): `needs_output_token_ids()=True` → real ids `[5] → [5,812] → …`; `False` → `[-1] → [-1,-1] → …`.

So moving `build_logitsprocs` back inside the warmup context is behavior-preserving and the gate still works as intended.

cc @njhill — this touches `/vllm/v1/sample` and `/vllm/v1/worker`, which you own in CODEOWNERS. Would appreciate a look when you have a moment.

Summary: under async scheduling, stateful logits processors that read output-token-id *values* saw `-1` placeholders because the `-1` repair gate was derived from `bool(custom_logitsprocs)` (missing builtin/plugin-registered processors, over-triggering for value-agnostic CLI ones). This replaces that heuristic with a declarative `LogitsProcessor.needs_output_token_ids()` (default `True`; the three in-tree builtins override to `False`), OR-aggregated across all loaded processors.

- Reporter @danbo610 reviewed and confirmed the approach, with production numbers under async + SynthID watermarking (8/8 detected, zero FP).
- `tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py` → 42 passed (incl. CUDA) + 2 new unit tests; async-scheduling e2e A/B posted above.

+class _StubLogitsProcessor(LogitsProcessor):
+    """Minimal no-op processor relying on the conservative default
+    (``needs_output_token_ids() == True``)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config, device, is_pin_memory):
+        pass
+
+    def is_argmax_invariant(self) -> bool:
+        return True
+
+    def update_state(self, batch_update) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def apply(self, logits):
+        return logits
+
+
+class _ValueAgnosticLogitsProcessor(_StubLogitsProcessor):
+    """Custom processor that opts out of output-token-id tracking."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def needs_output_token_ids(cls) -> bool:
+        return False
+
+
+def test_needs_output_token_ids_declarations():
+    """Builtins read at most the length of the output token ids, so they
+    declare no dependency; the base default stays conservative (True) for
+    out-of-tree processors."""
+    assert LogitsProcessor.needs_output_token_ids() is True
+    for cls in (
+        MinPLogitsProcessor,
+        LogitBiasLogitsProcessor,
+        MinTokensLogitsProcessor,
+    ):
+        assert cls.needs_output_token_ids() is False
+
+
+def test_build_logitsprocs_aggregates_output_token_ids_gate():
+    """``LogitsProcessors.needs_output_token_ids`` ORs the per-processor
+    declarations so async scheduling only repairs `-1` placeholders when a
+    loaded processor actually reads token values."""
+    device = torch.device("cpu")
+    vllm_config = VllmConfig()
+
+    builtins_only = build_logitsprocs(
+        vllm_config=vllm_config,
+        device=device,
+        is_pin_memory=PIN_MEMORY_AVAILABLE,
+        is_pooling_model=False,
+    )
+    assert builtins_only.needs_output_token_ids is False
+
+    value_agnostic = build_logitsprocs(
+        vllm_config=vllm_config,
+        device=device,
+        is_pin_memory=PIN_MEMORY_AVAILABLE,
+        is_pooling_model=False,
+        custom_logitsprocs=[_ValueAgnosticLogitsProcessor],
+    )
+    assert value_agnostic.needs_output_token_ids is False
+
+    value_reading = build_logitsprocs(
+        vllm_config=vllm_config,
+        device=device,
+        is_pin_memory=PIN_MEMORY_AVAILABLE,
+        is_pooling_model=False,
+        custom_logitsprocs=[_StubLogitsProcessor],
+    )
+    assert value_reading.needs_output_token_ids is True
+

| `False` (today's behavior for builtin-registered procs) | `[-1] → [-1, -1] → [-1, -1, -1] → …` | silently reads placeholders |

Both runs produce identical output text (the probe only observes), so this
isolates the output-token-id view. The `False` case reproduces the exact silent
failure from the issue; with the declaration wired through the gate, the async
`-1` repair runs and the processor sees real ids.

### Why this is a V1-runner fix (and V2 does not need the same change)

The V2 model runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) does not run
custom/plugin logits processors at all: `_get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features`
lists `"custom logits processors"` as unsupported whenever
`model_config.logits_processors` or a `vllm.logits_processors` entry point is
present (`vllm/config/vllm.py:2447-2450`), so those configs fall back to the V1
runner. The gate this PR fixes lives on the V1 path, which is exactly where such
processors execute. (The e2e forces `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` only because
`opt-125m` happens to default to V2; a real custom/plugin processor forces V1 on
its own.)

### Unit + regression

`python -m pytest tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py -v` → **42 passed**
(includes the CUDA `test_logitsprocs[...]` cases), plus the two added unit tests.
`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the touched files.

Good catch — fixed in 48c70dc. I moved `build_logitsprocs` back inside the `with self.jit_warmup_registry.activate():` block (right before the `InputBatch(...)` construction), so any warmup providers a processor's `__init__` registers are captured exactly as they were before this PR. The gate still reads `logitsprocs.needs_output_token_ids` — the only change vs. main is that the built object is now a local instead of an inline argument, and it's constructed within the same context.

No in-tree processor registers warmup providers today, but keeping construction inside the context makes it robust regardless, and avoids reasoning about registry internals.
